subtopics.title: Why VAT Exists and How It Works

questions.question: VAT is correctly described as:
options: An INDIRECT tax on consumption — borne by the final consumer, collected and paid over by businesses
A direct tax on company profits
A deduction from employees' salaries
A tax charged only on luxury imports

questions.question: Output tax and input tax are, in order:
options: Tax on exports and tax on imports
VAT charged on what the vendor SELLS, and VAT recovered on what the vendor BUYS
VAT on cash sales and VAT on credit sales
The standard rate and the zero rate

questions.question: The workshop buying timber at R400 and selling the table at R700 sends SARS the tax on:
options: R700 — the full selling price
R400 — the purchase price
R300 — the value its work added, being output tax less input tax
Nothing — furniture is zero-rated

questions.question: On the INVOICE basis, VAT is recognised:
options: Only once the customer settles the account
At the end of each financial year
When the goods leave the storeroom
The moment the invoice is issued, whether or not payment has happened

questions.question: Zero-rated supplies include:
options: Brown bread, maize meal, rice, samp, dried beans, milk, eggs, fresh fruit and vegetables, vegetable oil, paraffin — and exports
Residential rental and bank interest
Takeaway meals and cellphones
University fees and train fares

questions.question: Exempt supplies include:
options: Maize meal and fresh vegetables
Financial services where interest is earned, residential rental, public road and rail transport, and educational services
Exported goods
Courier deliveries

questions.question: The test that splits zero-rated from exempt is:
options: Whether the item is edible
Whether the price exceeds R500
Whether the SUPPLIER may recover its input tax — zero-rated is taxable at nought so inputs ARE recoverable; exempt is outside the system so they are NOT
Whether the buyer is a registered vendor

questions.question: A vendor dealing only in zero-rated goods will usually:
options: Owe SARS a large payment every period
Charge the standard rate regardless
Be barred from VAT registration
RECEIVE A REFUND — no output tax is charged while input tax on purchases is still recovered

questions.question: A desk is priced at R3 200 excluding VAT (rate 15%). The inclusive price is:
options: R3 680 — R3 200 plus VAT of R480, or R3 200 × 1,15

questions.question: An invoice totals R3 680 INCLUDING VAT. The VAT portion is:
options: R552 — fifteen percent of R3 680
R368 — ten percent of the total

questions.question: Stock costs R1 600, the mark-up is 75% on cost, and VAT is 15%. The customer pays:
options: R1 840 — cost plus VAT, then mark-up
R2 800 — VAT is never added to marked-up goods
R3 220 — mark up to R2 800 first, then add VAT

questions.question: When input tax for the period exceeds output tax, the vendor:
options: Pays the shortfall to SARS
Writes the difference off
Carries the difference as an operating expense
Is REFUNDABLE by SARS — the return produces a claim instead of a payment

questions.question: When a customer returns goods, the vendor:
options: Issues a CREDIT NOTE stating the VAT portion and reduces output tax by that amount
Keeps the output tax already declared
Claims the full selling price as input tax
Waits until year end to adjust

questions.question: When a debtor's account is written off as irrecoverable on the invoice basis:
options: The output tax already paid over is lost for good
The VAT portion of the written-off debt may be RECOVERED as input tax — and must be declared again if the debtor later pays
The entire debt becomes input tax
VAT is never affected by bad debts

questions.question: VAT gathered from customers is best described as:
options: Extra income of the business
A rebate on purchases
TRUST MONEY — the state's money held by the vendor until the return falls due
An interest-free loan from SARS

questions.question: The internal auditor's single searching question on input tax claims is:
options: Was the amount below R500?
Was the supplier a listed company?
Was the claim lodged before month end?
Does every claim stand on a VALID TAX INVOICE for a genuine BUSINESS purpose?

subtopics.title: The Line at the Bottom of the Slip

questions.question: The shop that charges you VAT:
options: Is a COLLECTOR, not an owner — it holds the money and passes it to SARS
Keeps the VAT as additional profit
Pays the VAT out of its own pocket
Shares the VAT with its suppliers

questions.question: Stacking every business's payment along the table's chain gives:
options: Three separate taxes on the same table
Exactly the tax on what the final consumer paid — each link taxed only on its own slice of value
More tax than the consumer paid
Nothing, since furniture is exempt

questions.question: What a registered business actually pays over each period is:
options: Every rand of VAT it collected
Fifteen percent of its profit
The GAP between what it collected and what it was charged
A flat monthly fee

subtopics.title: The Three Baskets at the Till

questions.question: The essentials basket is zero-rated because:
options: A tax on food punishes a poor household far harder — a family spending nearly everything on food would hand over the biggest share of its income
Food is cheap to farm
Retailers refuse to charge VAT on food
Fresh goods expire too quickly to tax

questions.question: Exports belong in the zero-rated basket because:
options: Exporters pay no taxes of any kind
The goods will be consumed in another country, and that country levies the tax instead
Export prices are fixed by treaty
Foreign customers cannot be invoiced

questions.question: The landlord letting out flats charges no VAT and:
options: Recovers the VAT on paint and plumbing
Charges VAT on repairs instead
Recovers NOTHING on what he paid — exempt supplies mean the input tax is simply swallowed
Receives a refund from SARS each period

questions.question: An ordinary brown loaf is zero-rated while a fancy artisanal loaf is not, which shows that:
options: The list is rewritten every month
Bakeries set their own rates
All bread is exempt
The list guards NECESSITIES, not tastes

subtopics.title: The Fifteen-on-One-Fifteen Trick, and Whose Money It Is

questions.question: The chant for the two directions is:
options: Going up, fifteen on a hundred; coming down, fifteen on a hundred and fifteen
Fifteen percent in both directions
Divide by fifteen going up, multiply coming down
Always take fifteen percent of the total

questions.question: Taking fifteen percent of an inclusive R3 680 gives R552, which is wrong because:
options: The rate is actually twelve percent
The fifteen percent was worked out on the SMALLER pre-tax price — R3 680 is already 115 parts
R3 680 includes a trade discount
VAT may never be calculated on totals

questions.question: On stock costing R1 600 sold at R3 220 inclusive, the R420 of VAT is:
options: Part of the shop's profit
A discount for the customer
SARS's money resting in the till until the return is due — the profit is the R1 200 mark-up
Commission owed to the supplier

questions.question: Charging customers "VAT" while not registered is:
options: Acceptable for small traders
A minor paperwork slip
Fine as long as the money is eventually paid over
Plain theft from the customer, who believes the money is travelling to SARS
